source.title: Beyond Top Words: MonoTM for Topic Modeling with Interpretable Monosemantic Features

record.tranche_reason: Applies corpus-trained SAEs to pretrained document embeddings and reports feature interpretability and cross-configuration results, but does not test the original toy-model geometry.
record.gate_note: The paper cites superposition as background but does not measure overlapping or nearly orthogonal directions, interference, or feature competition. Its topic-mixture and descriptor-comparison results do not directly test the listed claim versions. Rows record validated-feature counts and the cross-configuration feature-activation probe.
record.test_reason: RQ1 measures whether top-K SAEs trained on a pretrained LLM-based embedder's document embeddings recover features whose labels predict held-out activations (V4). An appendix probe of cross-configuration reconstructability bears weakly on V5. Neither toy-model geometry nor polysemanticity mechanisms are tested. The paper's main aim is topic modeling, but RQ1's results stand as a new-setting test of V4.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that corpus-trained SAEs on document embeddings yield relatively monosemantic, LLM-validated features, but their availability depends strongly on N and K. SAE activations also work well as pseudo-tokens for LDA mixture estimation, though the best configurations for the two roles differ. MonoTM decouples them, and excluded high-association features are mostly covered by validated descriptors or reflect format cues. The granularity probe is presented as a secondary, non-conclusive diagnostic.
record.recipe_differences: Trains top-K SAEs on pretrained text document embeddings and validates natural-language feature labels; it does not reproduce the original toy-network superposition method or measure its direction geometry.
record.method_sensitivity: Feature interpretability varies with activity level K, dictionary expansion N, and dataset. The authors also note dependence on Interpreter and Predictor LLMs and prompt details.

fits_no_version.finding: Restricting BoF+LDA to features with IS≥τ generally degrades document–topic mixture F1, more so at higher τ (Figs 6–8). Features that fail label validation still carry useful information.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE features that fail autointerpretability validation are not uninformative; interpretability and downstream usefulness diverge.

fits_no_version.finding: Topic-mixture quality with SAE bag-of-features peaks in a balanced band where N and K increase together. It is weak for wide dictionaries with tiny K and when mN=K (Fig 4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE configuration optimal for downstream statistical use differs from that optimal for interpretability.

record.problems: Feature interpretability is measured using Interpreter and Predictor LLMs, not human ground truth; the authors identify possible LLM blind spots. The cross-SAE probe uses a linear mapping, has no direct one-to-one feature matching, and is less conclusive on 20 Newsgroups. Results concern corpus-specific document embeddings, not general LLM internal activations.
record.rows_left_out: Tables 4–6 report many additional N, K, and interpretability-threshold combinations. Retained the IS ≥ 0.80 results for K = 4 and K = 32 across all listed N values, plus K = 8 and K = 16 at N = 0.5, to cover the reported configuration variation within the 60-row limit. Other thresholds and configurations are omitted; see Tables 4–6.

untested.parts: All of it: no toy networks, direction geometry, interference or sparsity transition.
All of it: no neuron polysemanticity or importance-versus-sharing analysis.
Internal LLM activations, spread of features across neurons, and any comparison of SAE features with neuron or embedding-dimension interpretability.
Completeness, stability across seeds or data, and one-to-one feature correspondence across dictionary sizes.
All of it: no comparison of 1-D with multi-dimensional features.

record.verdict_notes: The setting is SAEs on final document embeddings from an 8B LLM-based embedder, not residual-stream activations; treat the V4 support as indirect. Interpretability is judged by Gemma LLMs, not humans. Feature-count rows lack any baseline, such as interpretability of the raw 4096 embedding dimensions, so they cannot show SAE features are more monosemantic than the native basis.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test toy networks with more sparse features than dimensions, direction geometry, interference, a sparsity transition, or regular geometric structure.
Does not study neuron polysemanticity or whether feature importance determines dedicated versus shared dimensions.
Does not test whether polysemantic neurons arise without capacity pressure.
Studies corpus-trained SAE features in a pretrained document-embedding space, not feature distributions across neurons or internal activations of general LLMs.
Tests cross-configuration predictability of validated-feature activations, not whether SAE features are complete, canonical, or stable across training seeds, datasets, and other model types.
Uses individual SAE decoder features but does not compare one-dimensional directions with multidimensional features.

rows.check: This applies to all 42 feature-count rows (F20-*, W-*, R-*). There is no baseline such as raw embedding dimensions or random directions, so the counts show validated SAE features exist, not that they beat the neuron basis. The subject is document-level output embeddings of llama-embed-nemotron-8b, not internal activations. Validation is by an LLM Predictor (Gemma-3-12B).

rows.subject: Corpus-trained SAEs across 20 Newsgroups, Web of Science, and Reuters
rows.operation_detail: Compare the fraction of activated features passing validation across activity levels

conditions.value: 20 Newsgroups, Web of Science, and Reuters
evaluated K values; fraction averaged across evaluated N values

rows.measure: Fraction of activated features validated
rows.value: Decreases monotonically as K increases on all datasets
rows.note: The paper also states that larger K generally increases the absolute number of validated features at permissive thresholds.
rows.check: The value comes from text with no numbers. One worked example is given: at 20NG N=0.5, the dictionary-level fraction falls from 35.2% (K=8) to 13.8% (K=32). This is a dictionary-level fraction, whereas the text's monotonic claim concerns the activated-feature fraction averaged over N.

rows.subject: Cross-configuration SAE feature activations (20 Newsgroups)
rows.operation_detail: Ridge-regression linear mapping probe between validated-feature activation spaces
rows.measure: Median directional asymmetry Δ in normalized validation error; probability Δ < 0
rows.note: The interval includes zero; the authors say the aggregate asymmetry is less conclusive here. The probe does not establish one-to-one feature correspondence.
rows.check: The CI spans zero. A linear probe of reconstructability cannot by itself establish whether features are canonical.

rows.subject: Cross-configuration SAE feature activations (Web of Science)
rows.operation_detail: Ridge-regression linear mapping probe between validated-feature activation spaces
rows.measure: Median directional asymmetry Δ in normalized validation error; probability Δ < 0
rows.note: The asymmetry indicates greater reconstructability from higher- to lower-capacity configurations; authors caution it is not direct evidence of individual features splitting.
rows.check: The asymmetry shows configuration-dependent granularity only indirectly. Authors say it is not evidence of individual features splitting and gives no one-to-one matching.

rows.subject: Cross-configuration SAE feature activations (Reuters)
rows.operation_detail: Ridge-regression linear mapping probe between validated-feature activation spaces
rows.measure: Median directional asymmetry Δ in normalized validation error; probability Δ < 0
rows.note: The asymmetry indicates greater reconstructability from higher- to lower-capacity configurations; authors caution it is not direct evidence of individual features splitting.
rows.check: Same caveat as PROBE-WOS: an indirect linear-probe diagnostic, not a feature-matching measure of canonicity.

relationships.condition: Top-K SAEs on llama-embed-nemotron-8b document embeddings of 20NG, WoS and Reuters, IS≥0.80
relationships.reason: Hundreds to thousands of features per configuration have LLM-validated labels predicting held-out activation (count rows, e.g. W-K32-N4 = 5120, R-K4-N5 = 190). No neuron baseline is given.
relationships.display_finding: Each configuration gave hundreds to thousands of features whose LLM-validated labels predicted held-out activation, for example 5,120 in one configuration and 190 in another. No neuron baseline is given.

relationships.condition: Increasing per-document activity K, and dictionary size N at low K on 20NG and Reuters
relationships.reason: The validated fraction falls monotonically with K (KFRAC). At K=4, counts fall as N grows on 20NG (453 to 307) and Reuters (277 to 190), so recovery depends on SAE configuration and corpus.
relationships.display_finding: The validated fraction fell steadily as K increased, and at K=4 the number of validated features fell as N grew, from 453 to 307 on 20NG and from 277 to 190 on Reuters.

relationships.condition: Cross-configuration linear probes on Web of Science and Reuters
relationships.reason: Larger SAEs reconstruct smaller SAEs' validated activations better than the reverse (median Δ about −0.10, CIs exclude 0). This points to configuration-dependent granularity rather than a canonical basis; the evidence is indirect.
relationships.display_finding: Larger SAEs reconstructed smaller SAEs' validated activations better than the reverse (median Δ about −0.10, intervals excluding 0), indirect evidence that granularity depends on configuration rather than a canonical basis.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Validated SAE features in the tested document-embedding corpora and SAE settings
reader_labels.reason: The tables report features whose labels predict held-out activation behavior, with positive validated-feature counts across datasets and settings (feature-count rows).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Increasing per-document activity K across the three tested corpora
reader_labels.reason: The validated fraction decreases monotonically with K, although the absolute number of validated features can rise; interpretability depends on SAE configuration (KFRAC).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Cross-configuration probes on Web of Science and Reuters
reader_labels.reason: Higher-capacity feature activations linearly reconstruct lower-capacity validated-feature activations more easily in these datasets, indicating configuration-dependent granularity rather than a demonstrated invariant feature basis (PROBE-WOS, PROBE-REUTERS).
